page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.2xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance features 16.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The instance achieved average results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and PassMark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small blocks at 568.26 GB/sec, but drops to 92.39 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, while the PassMark memory score remains in the lower 25% tier.

This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads that leverage ARM64 architecture, such as static web serving, software compilation, and database operations, where it demonstrates average throughput. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, cryptographic operations, or large-scale language model inference due to weak single-core and encryption benchmark results. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated Ampere Altra cores offer a predictable compute-to-RAM ratio for distributed, scale-out workloads without the premium associated with x86 architectures.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.2xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated Ampere Altra vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps with no local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff: multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth are average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 14295.27 and 11.05 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-core performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core and PassMark CPU scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded ARM64 workloads, static web serving, and software compilation, offering a cost-efficient, dedicated resource profile for scale-out applications that do not require high single-threaded or cryptographic performance.
